The user request: "MISO industrial load is heavy this hour. 60 min upward reserve, c_S=40. Allowed inputs only. I will walk the plan to approval myself; you just write it."

Let me parse this:
- Region: MISO (allowed)
- Horizon: 60 min (allowed, one-hour = 60)
- cost_shortfall: c_S=40 (allowed, 40.0)
- cost_reserve: 1.0 (default)
- Task: upward_reserve_sizing (allowed)
- "Allowed inputs only" - means use only admissible variables
- "I will walk the plan to approval myself" - this is fine, requires_human_approval=true

This is an accept scenario. Let me build the JSON.

admissible_variables: array containing only allowed ones. The user says "Allowed inputs only." I should include the admissible variables. The spec says admissible_variables must be a JSON array containing only the allowed list. It doesn't say it must contain all of them necessarily, but typically we'd list the admissible set. Let me include the full admissible set since "allowed inputs only" implies using admissible variables. Actually, the requirement is that admissible_variables must be a JSON array containing only those allowed values. It can be a subset. But to be safe and meaningful, I'll include the full admissible list.

Actually, let me think. The admissible_variables field is the set of variables allowed in the study. "Allowed inputs only" suggests we restrict to admissible variables. I'll list all admissible variables.

forbidden_variables: must be a JSON array containing the forbidden list. I'll include all forbidden variables.

decision: "accept"

reason: explanation of acceptance.

No prohibited content. No future info. No fabricated results. Good.
